about: A box-pressed toro sold in a square tube, named after founder Nick Fusco's grandfather Gonzalo "Pepe" Torre. It is made for El Mago at Miguel Pinto's MGE Cigars Factory in Estelí.
notes: The maker calls it medium-strong; Cigar Coop rated it medium strength with medium to full body, and Neptune lists medium. Cigar Dojo and Cigar Coop listed Pepe among the 2022 debut cigars, but halfwheel dates the box-pressed tubo to May 2023.
verifyNotes: No field changes. Release year is disputed: September 2022 launch articles on Cigar Dojo and Cigar Coop list Pepe, while halfwheel's review table gives May 2023 and Neptune's first customer review is June 2023. Kept 2022 and tightened the note.

about: El Mago's first robusto, a box-pressed cigar with a Cameroon wrapper. The name is Spanish for mystical and refers to the bond between the founder's grandparents.
notes: Neptune says the Cameroon wrapper is capped at the head and foot with a lighter shade leaf. Cigar Dojo's 2022 launch list showed a Místico with a two-tone San Andrés wrapper; the Cameroon robusto shipped in 2023.
verifyNotes: No field changes. Reworded the note to attribute the 2022 two-tone Místico to Cigar Dojo (cigardojo.com/2022/09/el-mago-cigars-announces-company-debut/), since Cigar Coop's launch article from the same month gives that wrapper to the Miami Maduro instead.

about: El Mago's mild Connecticut toro, one of the brand's 2022 debut cigars and sold in tubes. The name is Spanish for triumphant.
notes: Retailers sell it as Triunfante Connecticut. The country the Corojo binder is grown in is not published.

about: The Habano-wrapped toro from El Mago's 2022 debut lineup, sold in tubes. Its packaging is modeled on The James Hotel, the Miami Beach Art Deco hotel the founder's grandfather owned.
notes: The maker and Neptune call it medium; Cigar Dojo listed it as mild-medium at launch.
verifyNotes: No field changes. The mild-medium launch listing in the note was confirmed on Cigar Dojo's September 2022 debut article, which is not in the sources list.

about: The maduro toro from El Mago's 2022 debut lineup, sold in tubes. It has a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over a Sumatra binder and filler from Estelí.
notes: The maker calls it medium to full; Neptune lists it as medium. The country the Sumatra binder is grown in is not published.
verifyNotes: Rewrote 'about' in plain words; it repeated the maker's sales pitch. Blend fields unchanged.

about: A Connecticut-wrapped toro in a tube, released in 2023 as a nod to Miami-Cuban culture. The founder's grandfather was born in Cuba.
notes: The maker and halfwheel call the wrapper Connecticut destapado without naming a country; Neptune lists it as U.S. Connecticut Shade. The medium strength comes from Neptune only.

about: El Mago's lancero, with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over a Criollo binder. Neptune says the name comes from a lotus flower painting by the founder's grandmother, Maria Torre.

verifyNotes: No field changes. No source gives a release year, so 'released' stays null; Neptune's first customer review is December 2023.

about: A thick 5 1/2 x 56 maduro that the maker bills as a bold, full-bodied smoke. Neptune describes it as the strongest cigar in the El Mago range.
notes: The maker calls it full-bodied and Neptune's write-up calls it the strongest El Mago, though Neptune's spec table lists medium.
verifyNotes: No field changes. No source gives a release year, so 'released' stays null. Neptune also lists the cigar as box-pressed, which the maker does not mention.

about: A 6 x 48 "thin toro" in a round tube with a Nicaraguan-grown Sumatra wrapper. It shipped in April 2024 in boxes of 14.

about: El Mago's first 6 x 60, sold in round tubes in boxes of 10. It is named for the disco era that shaped Miami nightlife when the founder's grandparents moved there.
notes: The maker and halfwheel say the binder is Criollo; Neptune's spec table says Corojo. The full strength comes from Neptune; the maker only calls it bold, spicy and smooth.

about: A small-batch 3 1/2 x 50 short robusto sold as a three-pack in a box made to look like a deck of cards. The box art shows a wizard lighting a cigar with a dragon's flame.

about: A box-pressed toro in a square tube that began shipping in summer 2025 as a regular production cigar. It is named after the old Jaguar the founder's grandmother drove him around in as a child.

about: A value-priced box-pressed robusto sold in 25-count bundles. The name recalls the founder smoking cigars on the beach with his grandfather.

about: The first release in El Mago's Collectible Tin Series, a 5 x 50 box-pressed robusto that shipped in March 2026. The series was inspired by a vintage tobacco tin the founder found while thrifting.
